newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firm ahead of EU tender.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firm ahead of EU tender.

text.p: French physical wheat markets were firm but nervous on Thursday, with the scramble for EU licences dominating sentiment, traders said.

Maize fell, suffering from Wednesday's EU decision to allow the sale of genetically-modified maize. It may herald the early shipment of supplies under Spain's annual quota of preferential imports from the the United States, traders said.
The imports are expected to hit French maize trade.
"The wheat market is driven by buyers," one broker said.
Wheat delivered at Rouen was quoted up five francs per tonne for January, with February/March at 855 francs.
Wheat fob Creil was at 800 francs for January, unchanged.
Maize fell 10 francs a tonne across the board. Bordeaux deliveries were quoted at 850 francs per tonne, with maize fob Atlantic ports at 875 francs.
French grain prices exclude twice-monthly carrying charges which, for example, are 36.36 francs per tonne for late December and 39.99 francs for first-half January.
Traders have applied through France for licences to export 725,550 tonnes of soft wheat at a broad range of rebates between 7.49 and 17.44 Ecus per tonne.
The lowest subsidy bid, at 7.49 Ecus per tonne for 40,000 tonnes, is equivalent to $166 per tonne fob France for January loading, exporters reckoned.
"Just like last week, the tonnage shows the market is short export licences and the level of bids shows a desire to squeeze the market," one operator said.
In the past week, some exporters have accused others of wanting to make capital out of the shortage of licences.
